findings.title: An older failed refresh can invalidate a newer passive observation
findings.rationale: Nonblocking under the severe-runtime threshold. In web-app/src/telas/Modelos.tsx:786, atualizarStatus dispatches unavailable using only the remote ID after completeMeaningfulIntent succeeds. The reducer then marks the currently cached observation unavailable without comparing failure authority with its persisted fence. A feasible ordering is: an individual refresh commits failure at fence 2 and its real 409 response is held; another authorized client persists successful APPROVED evidence at fence 3; an already pending passive catalogue GET delivers fence 3 to this screen; the held failure is then released. Passive adoption does not advance completedIntent, so the older intent remains admissible and invalidates the newer fence-3 observation, including its editor proof. No derived read follows this catch. The catalogue failure branch has the analogous unconditional catalogFailure veto. The new successful-response race cases and the existing newer-failure-versus-older-success case do not cover this reverse ordering. This is a source-derived counterexample, not an executed reproduction, and creates a conservative availability false-negative rather than demonstrated unauthorized use or server exhaustion.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): add a real-BFF regression holding the completed failure response until newer persisted success arrives through a passive read, then implement reviewed failure-authority comparison within the existing observation owner while preserving genuinely current unavailability. B: if the current safe error response lacks sufficient context/fence information, obtain a bounded HOW/contract review for that metadata instead of inferring authority from arrival order or suppressing every failure. C: explicitly defer the conservative false-negative with a named owner, recovery limitation and follow-up. Keep this nonblocking for the performance lane and preserve the existing opposite-order failure assertions.
